user.title: Connect to Arcane
user.description: Enter the address of your Arcane instance and an API key created under Settings → API keys.

data_description.url: Full address of the Arcane web interface, for example http://192.168.1.10:3552
data_description.api_key: An Arcane API key. It needs read access plus permission for the actions you want to control from Home Assistant.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off if Arcane uses a self-signed certificate.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Arcane
reauth_confirm.description: The API key for {url} is no longer accepted. Enter a new one.

data_description.api_key: Leave empty to keep the key that is already stored.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to Arcane. Check the URL and that the instance is reachable.
error.insufficient_permissions: The API key is missing the environments:list permission.
error.invalid_url: That is not a valid http:// or https:// address.

abort.already_configured: This Arcane instance is already configured.

data_description.scan_interval: How often Arcane is polled, in seconds.
data_description.environments: Leave empty to follow every environment Arcane exposes.
data_description.monitor_containers: Create a device with entities for each container.
data_description.monitor_projects: Create a device with entities for each Compose project.
data_description.monitor_resources: Poll the image, volume and network counts and the Docker version.
data_description.host_stats: Take one sample per update over a short lived WebSocket. Off by default because it is an extra connection per update.
data_description.include_internal: Also expose containers Arcane marks as internal.
data_description.include_hidden: Also expose containers hidden in the Arcane interface.

data.entity_prefix: Prefix device names with their kind
data.events: Fire events on the Home Assistant bus

data_description.update_entities: Offer an update entity per container that redeploys it onto the newer image.
data_description.health_sensors: Add a Healthy sensor to containers that define a health check.
data_description.entity_prefix: Name devices Container x and Project x so a container and a project of the same name do not collide. Entity IDs that already exist keep their current name.
data_description.nest_containers: Show a container as a child device of the Compose project it belongs to.
data_description.events: Fire arcane_container_state_changed, arcane_container_health_changed and arcane_project_state_changed so automations can react to crashes and health changes.

data_description.allow_control: Turn this off for a read only setup: no switches, buttons or update installs are created.
data_description.redeploy_buttons: Add a button per container and per project that pulls the image again and recreates it.
data_description.prune_button: Add a button per environment that removes unused images, networks and build cache. Containers and volumes are never pruned.

options.dangling: Dangling images, unused networks and build cache
options.unused: All unused images, networks and build cache

container_not_found.message: Container {name} is no longer known to Arcane.
